title: Package, universal conversation model and local store (`checkpoint init`)
acceptance: `pip install -e .` in the project succeeds with only the standard library as a runtime dependency (`mcp` appears only under an optional extra, e.g. `[project.optional-dependencies] mcp`), and afterwards both `checkpoint --help` and `python -m ai_checkpoint --help` exit 0 and list the subcommands init, capture, save, list, show, resume
`python -c "import ai_checkpoint"` and importing the engine/capture/resume modules succeeds in an environment where `mcp` is NOT installed

Conversation and Message model objects round-trip: building a Conversation (conversation_id, provider, created_at, messages[id, role, content, timestamp]) and serialising to JSON then loading it back yields an equal object; the JSON keys match MVP section 9 (`conversation_id`, `provider`, `created_at`, `messages` with `id`, `role`, `content`, `timestamp`)

In an empty temp directory, `checkpoint init` exits 0 and creates `.ai-checkpoint/` containing `config.json`, `conversations/`, `checkpoints/`, `state/`, a `.gitignore`, and a git repository (`git -C .ai-checkpoint rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds) with at least one initial commit
The `.gitignore` written by init excludes credential-like files (at minimum `*.env`/`.env*`, `*.key`, `*.pem`, `secrets*`), and `config.json` contains no API keys or tokens

Running `checkpoint init` a second time in the same directory exits 0, prints that it is already initialised, and does not delete or alter existing conversations/checkpoints or git history (commit count unchanged)
Running `checkpoint list` (or save/capture) in a directory with no `.ai-checkpoint/` exits non-zero with a message telling the user to run `checkpoint init`, without a Python traceback

The store location defaults to `./.ai-checkpoint` and can be overridden with a global `--root DIR` option (or `AI_CHECKPOINT_ROOT` env var); `checkpoint --root /tmp/x init` creates `/tmp/x/.ai-checkpoint`
A test suite exists under `tests/` and `python -m pytest -q` passes offline

title: Capture a Claude Code JSONL transcript into the working buffer (`checkpoint capture --transcript`)
acceptance: Realistic fixture transcripts exist under `tests/fixtures/` following docs/research.md: user/assistant lines with `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `sessionId`, `timestamp`, `cwd`, `message`; string and block-list content; `tool_use`, `tool_result` and `thinking` blocks; an assistant turn split across several lines sharing one `message.id`; and unknown line types (`summary`, `system`, `file-history-snapshot`)

`checkpoint capture --transcript tests/fixtures/<file>.jsonl` exits 0, writes `.ai-checkpoint/conversations/<sessionId>.json` in the universal format with `provider` = `claude_code` and `conversation_id` = the transcript's `sessionId`, updates `state/current.json` to point at that conversation, and prints how many messages were captured/added

Test 1 (MVP section 17): for a fixture with exactly 50 human/assistant messages (25 user prompts, 25 assistant replies, some assistant replies split across multiple lines and some interleaved with tool_use/tool_result), the captured conversation contains every user and assistant message exactly once, in transcript order, with text content identical to the source, each message's `timestamp` equal to the source line's timestamp, and the correct session ID: 100% recovery, 0 duplicates, 0 missing
Assistant lines sharing a `message.id` are merged into ONE assistant message whose text is the in-order concatenation of their text blocks; `thinking` blocks are not included in content

A `user` line whose content is only `tool_result` blocks is NOT recorded as a human `user` message (it is either stored with role `tool` or attached to the preceding assistant tool call); `tool_use` blocks are preserved in structured form (tool name and input) on the assistant message and not dropped silently
Lines of unknown `type`, blank lines and a truncated/invalid final JSON line are skipped without failing; capture exits 0 and the valid messages are stored
Capturing the same transcript twice is idempotent: the second run reports 0 new messages and the conversation file's message list is unchanged (dedup by source uuid / message.id)
Restart/recovery: capturing the first N lines, then capturing the full (appended) transcript, yields exactly the same conversation as capturing the full transcript once

Secrets are redacted before anything is written: a fixture message containing an Anthropic key (`sk-ant-...`), an OpenAI-style key (`sk-...`), a GitHub token (`ghp_...`), an AWS access key id (`AKIA...`) and an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header is stored with each secret replaced by a `[REDACTED...]` marker; `grep -r` for the original secret strings under `.ai-checkpoint/` finds nothing; ordinary text in the same message is unchanged
`checkpoint capture --transcript does-not-exist.jsonl` exits non-zero with a clear error and no traceback, and leaves the store unchanged

title: Continuous capture via Claude Code hooks (`capture --from-hook`, `install-hooks`)
acceptance: `echo '{"session_id":"<id>","transcript_path":"<fixture path>","cwd":"<dir>","hook_event_name":"Stop"}' | checkpoint capture --from-hook` reads the hook JSON from stdin, syncs the transcript at `transcript_path` into the working buffer, and exits 0

Simulated continuous capture: a test that appends a transcript fixture to a temp JSONL file in several chunks and invokes `capture --from-hook` (as Stop / UserPromptSubmit events) after each chunk ends with a conversation identical to a one-shot capture of the full file, with no duplicates

The hook path never breaks the host agent: malformed stdin JSON, a missing `transcript_path`, or a transcript file that does not exist each make `capture --from-hook` exit 0 (with at most a message on stderr) and leave the store unchanged

`checkpoint install-hooks` writes/merges `.claude/settings.json` in the project directory so that `Stop`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreCompact` and `SessionEnd` each run `checkpoint capture --from-hook`, and `SessionStart` runs the resume-injection hook command (F-005), using the config shape `{"hooks":{"Stop":[{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"..."}]}]}}`; the output file is valid JSON
`checkpoint install-hooks` preserves existing unrelated keys and existing hook entries in a pre-existing `.claude/settings.json`, and running it twice does not add duplicate entries

title: Checkpoints with git history (`checkpoint save`, `list`, `show`)
acceptance: After capturing a fixture, `checkpoint save "forecasting-v1"` exits 0, writes `.ai-checkpoint/checkpoints/cp-001.json`, and prints output in the shape of MVP section 30: `Checkpoint created:` followed by `cp-001`, and `Git commit:` followed by the short commit hash

The checkpoint JSON contains `checkpoint_id`, `name`, `conversation_id`, `provider`, `created_at`, `messages` (a full snapshot of the current conversation's messages), `state` with keys `objective`, `decisions`, `completed_work`, `open_questions`, `next_steps`, `artifacts` (empty list) and `metadata`

Each save creates exactly one new commit in the `.ai-checkpoint` repo with subject `checkpoint: cp-NNN - <name>` and the checkpoint file in that commit; the short hash printed by save equals `git -C .ai-checkpoint log -1 --format=%h`
Checkpoint IDs increase sequentially (`cp-001`, `cp-002`, `cp-003`) and are never reused

Test 2 (MVP section 18): with a 60-message fixture captured incrementally, saving after messages 1-20, 21-40 and 41-60 gives cp-001 with exactly messages 1-20, cp-002 with 1-40 and cp-003 with 1-60; after all three saves, `cp-001.json` and `cp-002.json` are byte-identical to their content in the commits that created them (`git -C .ai-checkpoint diff <cp-001 commit> HEAD -- checkpoints/cp-001.json` is empty)

`checkpoint list` prints one line per checkpoint in order, each with the ID and name (e.g. `cp-001   forecasting-v1`) plus created time; with no checkpoints it prints a 'no checkpoints' message and exits 0

`checkpoint show cp-001` prints the checkpoint's metadata (id, name, conversation id, provider, created_at, message count, commit hash) and `checkpoint show cp-001 --json` prints valid JSON of the stored checkpoint
`checkpoint show cp-999` and `checkpoint resume cp-999` exit non-zero with a 'checkpoint not found' message and no traceback
`checkpoint save "x"` when nothing has been captured yet exits non-zero with a clear message and creates no checkpoint file or commit
Previous checkpoint versions are retrievable from git: `git -C .ai-checkpoint log --oneline` lists one `checkpoint:` commit per saved checkpoint
No secrets reach git: after capturing the secret-bearing fixture and saving, `git -C .ai-checkpoint log -p --all` contains none of the original secret strings

title: Resume context and SessionStart injection (`checkpoint resume`)
acceptance: `checkpoint resume cp-001` exits 0, prints `Checkpoint loaded.` (to stderr or as a header line) and prints a resume context to stdout that begins with `You are continuing work from checkpoint cp-001` and includes the checkpoint name, an objective section, sections for decisions / completed work / open questions / next steps (showing 'none recorded' or omitted when empty), and a `RELEVANT CONVERSATION HISTORY` section

The history section contains every user and assistant message of the checkpoint, in order, labelled by role, with full text (raw history, no compression): for the 50-message fixture each of the 50 message texts appears in the output exactly once and in the original order

The objective defaults to the first human user message of the checkpoint when no explicit objective was recorded; `checkpoint save NAME --objective TEXT --next-step TEXT` (repeatable `--next-step`) stores these in `state` and they appear in the resume output
`checkpoint resume cp-001 --out ctx.md` writes the same context to the file, which a user can paste into a new conversation
Resuming cp-001 after cp-002 and cp-003 exist produces context containing only cp-001's messages (none from later checkpoints)

`checkpoint resume cp-001 --on-next-start` records a pending resume; then piping a SessionStart hook payload (`{"session_id":...,"hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"startup",...}`) into the SessionStart hook command prints JSON of the form `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"<resume context for cp-001>"}}` and exits 0; a second SessionStart invocation prints nothing (pending resume consumed)
The SessionStart hook command with no pending resume, or with malformed stdin, exits 0 and prints nothing to stdout

title: Optional MCP server exposing checkpoint tools
acceptance: A server module (e.g. `ai_checkpoint.mcp.server`) defines tools `save_checkpoint(name)`, `list_checkpoints()`, `get_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)` and `resume_checkpoint(checkpoint_id)` whose underlying functions can be called in-process in a test without starting a transport

In-process: `save_checkpoint` after a capture returns `{"checkpoint_id": "cp-001", "commit": "<hash>"}` and creates the same file and git commit as the CLI; `list_checkpoints` returns a list of `{"id","name","created_at"}`; `get_checkpoint` returns the checkpoint's metadata/state; `resume_checkpoint` returns the same resume context text as `checkpoint resume`
`get_checkpoint` / `resume_checkpoint` with an unknown ID return or raise a clear 'checkpoint not found' error rather than crashing the server

If `mcp` is pip-installable in the sandbox: after `pip install -e .[mcp]`, launching the server over stdio (e.g. `checkpoint mcp` or `python -m ai_checkpoint.mcp.server`) and sending MCP `initialize` + `tools/list` returns exactly the four tool names above with input schemas; a `tools/call` of `list_checkpoints` succeeds
Without `mcp` installed, `checkpoint mcp` exits non-zero with a message saying to install the `mcp` extra, and all other CLI commands still work
